_comment: Canonical list of websites used to find major medical / health care fraud cases (Medicare, Medicaid and commercial payers). Edit this file to add, remove or disable a source; the scrapers read it at run time. 'key' maps to a discovery module in fraudscrape/discovery/ and to the folder name used under ./downloaded/.

sources.name: U.S. Department of Justice (Main Justice + all 93 U.S. Attorney's Offices)
sources.why: Primary publisher of federal health care fraud criminal charges, convictions, sentencings, False Claims Act civil settlements and the annual National Health Care Fraud Takedowns. Covers Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE and private/commercial insurers.

harvest.method: official JSON API, paginated newest-first, then filtered on the 'Healthcare Fraud' topic tag and on health-care-fraud keywords
harvest.notes: justice.gov HTML is behind an Akamai bot-manager interstitial, so pages are fetched with headless Chrome; if that fails the press release is rebuilt from the API 'body' field. PDF attachments (indictments, complaints, settlement agreements) are downloaded as well.

sources.name: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Inspector General
sources.why: Publishes the government-wide enforcement-action database (criminal, civil and Civil Monetary Penalty actions, including state Medicaid Fraud Control Unit cases), audits and evaluations of Medicare/Medicaid improper payments, and the LEIE exclusions list.

harvest.method: paginated HTML listings (20 items/page, newest first) walked until the coverage cut-off date; reports are keyword-filtered and their full-text PDFs are downloaded too

sources.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation (national + 55 field offices)
sources.why: Lead investigative agency for federal health care fraud; field-office press releases cover cases against Medicare, Medicaid and private/commercial insurers.

harvest.method: full site sitemap is downloaded and every /news/press-releases/ and field-office press-release URL is keyword-matched, then each candidate page is fetched and filtered on its published date

sources.name: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
sources.why: Payer-side program-integrity announcements, Medicare/Medicaid improper-payment and fraud-prevention reporting, provider-enrollment moratoria and Strike Force partnership news.

harvest.method: newsroom sitemap is downloaded and press releases / fact sheets / news alerts are keyword-matched, then fetched with headless Chrome (cms.gov blocks plain HTTP clients) and filtered on published date

sources.name: U.S. Government Accountability Office
sources.why: Independent audits and testimony on Medicare/Medicaid fraud risk, improper payments and program-integrity oversight - useful context documents for the case corpus.

harvest.method: faceted reports-and-testimonies listing browsed with headless Chrome (gao.gov blocks plain HTTP clients); each product page plus its full-text PDF is saved

considered_but_not_scraped.name: NHCAA (National Health Care Anti-Fraud Association)
considered_but_not_scraped.reason: Commercial-payer case material is behind a members-only login; only high-level statistics are public.

considered_but_not_scraped.name: State Medicaid Fraud Control Unit websites (50 states)
considered_but_not_scraped.reason: State MFCU press releases are already syndicated into the HHS-OIG enforcement database, which is scraped instead.

considered_but_not_scraped.name: PACER / CourtListener dockets
considered_but_not_scraped.reason: Underlying court filings are useful but require per-document fees or a separate API key; DOJ press-release attachments cover the key filings.
